transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-05 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Romero (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood), Jordan Ruiz (Blue Lantern CTO), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Sam Ortega (Infra), Evan Cho (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Customer evaluating reserved capacity for latency-sensitive feature set; high interest in warm pools, prewarming, and strong tenancy isolation. Follow-up SE-run benchmark and pricing doc promised.

00:00 Jordan (Blue Lantern): "Okay, thanks everyone for joining. We're excited — we run inference for our realtime annotator and the cold starts have been killing our p99. So main goal today is to figure out whether reserved GPUs on Redwood will give us the latency tail guarantees without us having to manage kernels ourselves."

00:28 Alex (Redwood AE): "Great, Jordan. Quick intros — I'm Alex, AE; Maya's our SE who will own the benchmark and latency profiling. High level, Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, warm pool prewarm options, and VPC connectivity if you need it. But let's get into your workload first. Priya, can you give us the traffic shape?"

00:46 Priya (Blue Lantern): "Yeah, so our annotator is called 'Beacon' — it gets variable traffic, base QPS is ~300, peaks to 4,200 qps during certain campaign windows — those are short, like 10-30 minutes, but the p99 jumps from ~120ms to 1.6s which is unacceptable. We also run some larger context requests for multimodal scoring that need more memory."

01:18 Maya (Redwood SE): "Okay mm-hmm, that delta is what prewarm + warm pool is for. We can reserve a hot pool of nodes that keep model KV caches warm and we can prewarm more nodes on burst. The tradeoff is cost for idle prewarmed capacity vs cold-start tail. Do you have constraints on how long a request can be queued?"

01:39 Sam (Blue Lantern): "We try to keep tail under 300ms, anything above 500ms triggers client-side retries which compounds the load. We have strict SLOs with internal customers. Also, security is non-negotiable — we need KMS with customer-managed keys and audit logs. SOC2 is a must for procurement."

02:05 Liam (Redwood): "Right, for Dedicated we support VPC peering + customer-managed KMS integrations; audit logs are available via the Console and can be exported to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 package and the KMS integration doc after the call."

02:28 Jordan: "One of our concerns is cross-tenant blast radius. We can't have noisy neighbors; does Redwood guarantee node-level isolation or do we need fully dedicated nodes per tenant?"

02:50 Maya: "We offer dedicated pools that are isolated to your account. Within that pool, we do tenant fencing across pods; if you need stricter isolation we can map to dedicated nodes per tenant or even per environment. There's a cost delta. Also, warming strategy: we keep KV cache in memory to avoid expensive recompute on tokens. In some cases we recommend quantized variants for cost savings."

03:30 Priya: "Quantized variants — do you see model quality drop for our scoring models? We need deterministic outputs for certain flavors of scoring."

03:43 Maya: "For scoring we usually recommend FP16 or int8-quant with a calibration pass — we can run evals on your prompt set in the pilot. If determinism is critical we can keep higher precision for those routes and quantize the rest."

04:10 Evan (Blue Lantern): "What about failover — if our reserved pool is exhausted during a spike, will traffic fail or fall back to hosted Redwood models?"

04:24 Alex: "You can configure routing policies: strict (reject when no capacity), flexible (fallback to hosted variant), or staged (queue briefly then fallback). Most customers use staged fallback with canary ratio during ramp windows. We'll work with you on manifests for explicit fallback rules."

04:52 Jordan: "Costs — can you walk us through how prewarm hours vs burst billing works? We need to compare to our current self-hosted GPU spend."

05:10 Maya: "Sure. Reserved nodes are charged as committed units (monthly), warm pool prewarm is a smaller hourly charge while a node is kept in hot state, and burst usage beyond reservation is charged at on-demand rates. There's also an opt-in 'preemptible' burst lane with lower cost but possible preemption. We'll send a pricing template. Note: billing is per-VM / per-GPU, not per-token for Dedicated."

05:39 Sam: "Do you expose token-level cost and tracing? We want to attribute cost to routes and teams."

05:50 Liam: "Yes, Console has token-level breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and tracing links you can pipe to your APM. We'll demo that in the deep dive."

06:10 Jordan: "Can you do VPC peering to our prod VPC? We have strict egress rules and want traffic to stay inside our network."

06:22 Alex: "Yes, VPC peering or PrivateLink-style connectivity is available for Dedicated and Private options. For on-prem we have an appliance path as well, though that adds extra lead time. Which is your preference?"

06:36 Jordan: "Prefer peering to keep low latency. On-prem is a last resort."

06:45 Priya: "Pilot idea: can we run a 2-hour window with synthetic peak traffic and our real prompt set to measure p50/p95/p99 with prewarm params?"

06:56 Maya: "Absolutely. Typical flow: we provision a small reserved pool sized for your baseline, then prewarm for peak windows you share, run the synthetic traffic, gather traces and tail latencies, then iterate on prewarm thresholds. We'll draft a plan and send it."

07:20 Jordan: "How quickly can you provision reserved nodes? Week? Days?"

07:28 Maya: "For hosted Dedicated pools it's usually 48-72 hours to reserve standard nodes, expedited for enterprise. If you need specific hardware (A100 vs H100) lead times vary with supply. We'll confirm when we know target region and SKU."

07:46 Sam: "What about burst limits — like if we have a sudden 10x spike, do you autoscale? How long to spin new nodes from cold?"

08:00 Maya: "Autoscale respects your policy: conservatively we add nodes based on queue depth; spinning a fresh node has cold-start penalty — that's where warm pool and prewarming help. New node spin can be anywhere from 30s to a few minutes depending on image pull and model load. With prewarm we can get sub-200ms tail for most gen models. But we need to test with your exact models and sequence lengths."

08:28 Priya: "Sequence lengths — we have both short chat-like inputs and longer 2k token scoring runs. Do you optimize kernels per sequence length?"

08:41 Maya: "Yes, runtime picks kernels and execution path based on sequence length distribution. We'll profile both workloads in the pilot; for long contexts we might suggest a different model variant or partitioning to avoid huge KV overhead."

09:05 Evan: "Procurement question: SOC2 + ISO? We have an external auditor who will need docs."

09:15 Liam: "We can provide SOC2 Type II artifacts and ISO certs, plus a redacted architecture diagram and the compliance contact. We'll include that in the docs pack."

09:30 Jordan: "What about data residency? Some of our campaigns are EU-only."

09:37 Alex: "You can pin Dedicated capacity to a region. For Private on-prem we obviously stay in your datacenter. We'll note regional availability for H100/A100 in the pricing sheet."

09:52 Priya: "A nit: if we roll out can we do canary routing so only a fraction of traffic hits the Dedicated pool initially?"

10:00 Maya: "Yes, Redwood's routing supports per-route weights; you can split by percent or by route. You can also schedule canaries during off-peak for safe rollouts."

10:17 Sam: "We need to be explicit on monitoring — alert thresholds at p99, token failures, and queue depth. Does Redwood emit those metrics to Prometheus?"

10:29 Liam: "We expose metrics to both Prometheus and your cloud metrics backend (CloudWatch/GCM). We'll provide a starter dashboard config."

10:40 Jordan: "Okay, last thing on security: KMS — can we keep keys in our KMS (AWS KMS) and have Redwood integrate?"

10:50 Maya: "Yes, customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated & Private via our KMS bridge; we'll need an IAM role/bookkeeping to allow envelope encryption. We'll attach the KMS integration doc after the call."

11:05 Priya: "Anything you need from us today to move this forward?"

11:10 Alex: "If you can share a 7-day qps histogram and a set of 10 representative prompts for evaluation we'll prep the pilot. Also which region and preferred GPU SKU. We'll send the SOW and pricing with options: baseline reserved + warm pool / reserved + smaller warm pool + higher fallback to hosted."

11:32 Jordan: "Sounds good. We also want an estimate of cost delta vs us self-hosting. I'll loop Finance in once we have the pricing template."

11:45 Maya: "One more practical note: if you want deterministic scoring at scale, sometimes we recommend pinning model variant for that route to avoid quantization drift — we can add that to the evaluation plan."

12:00 Alex: "Great. Quick recap of next steps: Alex sends pricing & SOW, Maya drafts pilot and prewarm params, Sam shares traffic histograms, Jordan confirms security contacts. We'll aim to schedule the pilot next week if timelines align."

12:22 Jordan: "Thanks, everyone. Appreciate the clarity — look forward to the docs."

12:30 (call ends)
